direction.name: The sentence is the layout
direction.idea: One short sentence, set at poster scale, is the composition. The trick that makes it an idea rather than a big headline: something from the subject sits inside the sentence where a word would be. A strip of photograph fills the gap between two words; a small live fragment of the product replaces the noun; the object the sentence names is pictured at the size of a letter. Write the sentence first, find the word that can be shown instead of said, and put the showing in its place. The reader completes the sentence with their eyes.
direction.composition: The sentence is four to seven words and runs as one or two full-width lines at 9–13vw. Inline with the type, on the baseline, sits one media slot: a rounded-rectangle or square frame exactly one line-height tall and two to three ems wide, holding a photograph or a looping crop. Above and below the sentence the screen is empty except for a small navigation line and one supporting sentence set small, both on the same left margin. Later sections repeat the grammar at smaller scale: each is a short statement on the left six columns with its proof (image, figure, list) on the right, so the page reads as a series of sentences with evidence. Generous vertical space (160px or more) between sections.
direction.typography: Display weight with real presence (medium to bold), tracking -0.03 to -0.05em, leading 0.95–1.0 so two lines sit close. The inline frame aligns to cap height and baseline exactly; set it with em units so it scales with the type.
direction.colour: A calm ground with ink at full contrast. The only colour comes from the photograph inside the sentence; if the palette has an accent, use it once, on the action.
direction.imagery: One strong, simple photograph that reads at small size (a face, an object, a texture, a horizon), cropped to a wide strip inside the sentence. The same image may open to full width in the next section, so the small slot feels like a window onto something larger.
direction.richness: The collision of big type and one live image inside it. Because there is only one image on the first screen, choose it with care and give it perfect alignment to the letters.
direction.pitfalls: The sentence must be short enough for two lines on a phone, where the inline frame drops to its own line between the two halves. Do not style one word differently to fake the device. Do not use more than one slot per sentence.

hero.name: Title in the sky, line on the horizon
hero.blueprint: One wide photograph or render fills the viewport, chosen with the subject in the lower 55% and open sky, fog or a plain wall above it. The headline is centred in that empty upper zone: two lines at clamp(72px, 7.2vw, 112px), leading 0.9, its cap line 72px from the top, the first line short and the second longer so the block widens towards the subject. On the horizon, with its baseline at 52% of the height, one supporting sentence is split into two halves at 22px: the first half right-aligned to end at column 5, the second left-aligned from column 8, so the subject shows through the 260px gap between them. Wordmark top-left on a 32px margin; up to three text links from column 9; the single action top-right as a solid rectangle in the paper colour. All type is in one ink chosen against the sky; on a pale sky use the photograph's darkest tone rather than black. Nothing else crosses the lower half.
hero.mobile: The picture is re-cropped to portrait with the subject in the lower 45%. The headline sits centred in the sky at 11vw on two lines, 96px down, and the two halves of the sentence become two centred lines at 17px directly under it. The action is a full-width button 24px above the bottom edge on a neutral scrim band 96px tall. Wordmark top-left and a menu word top-right.
hero.headline: Two lines, the second the longer, at most about 14 characters per line: the name of the place, or a 3–5 word claim about it.

type.note: A narrow, sharp display serif for headlines against a small plain sans: a five-to-one jump with nothing between. Suits agencies, bakeries and restaurants, fashion and editorial brands.

palette.name: Greys and mint
palette.note: White, near-black and two greys fill a board of flat tiles. Mint floods a few whole tiles (one statement, one figure, the closing call to action) and appears nowhere else.

motion.name: Shutter image
motion.description: The one hero or showcase image opens from an edge with a clip-path over about 1.1 seconds while the picture inside settles from 1.12 scale to rest. Use it once, on the image that matters most; later images simply are there. Recipe: 'Image shutter' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Paragraph with picture words
sections.blueprint: One paragraph does the work of a feature grid. Three or four sentences, 35–50 words in total, set at clamp(30px, 3.6vw, 60px), leading 1.18, medium weight, across columns 1–11, left-aligned. Each sentence names one capability, and directly after that capability's key noun sits an inline slot: an inline-block frame 1em tall and 1.9em wide, radius 0.18em, dropped 0.12em below the baseline, holding a tight photograph crop (object-fit: cover) or a real interface control at readable size. Four slots at most, never two on one line. The nouns keep the weight and colour of the rest; the slots are the only emphasis. Mark it up as a paragraph and give the section a visually hidden heading of two or three words; nothing visible sits above. 72px lower, starting at column 7, one supporting sentence at 18px and the action.
sections.mobile: The paragraph drops to 7vw with leading 1.22 and fills the width. Slots stay inline at 1em tall but narrow to 1.5em wide. If a slot lands alone at the start of a line, let it; do not shrink the type. The supporting sentence and the action follow at full width.

sections.name: One frame, three distances
sections.blueprint: A wrapper 300vh tall holds a sticky stage of 100svh. On the stage one frame is centred: 30vw wide at 4:5, square corners, overflow hidden. Inside it the same photograph is shown at three distances as the reader scrolls: the whole subject, then scaled to 180% toward one detail, then to 320% on a second detail (transform: scale with a transform-origin per stage, 700ms ease, switched by IntersectionObserver on three invisible markers). The sentence is delivered in halves: its first two or three words sit above the frame at clamp(56px, 8vw, 130px), centred; the last words arrive below the frame at the second stage, overlapping the frame's bottom edge by 0.3em. At the third stage one caption of 28ch at 17px appears to the right of the frame, top-aligned. The two halves together are the heading and stay within two lines.
sections.mobile: The frame grows to 70vw at 4:5 and stays sticky at centre. The first half of the sentence sits above it at 13vw, the second half below it at the same size. The third-stage caption appears under the sentence at 16px, centred.

sections.name: Lines that step across
sections.blueprint: The sequence is written, not counted. Four lines of display type, one stage per line, each a complete short clause that begins with its order word: 'First you send it.' 'Then we take it apart.' 'You choose one.' 'It ships on Friday.' Set at clamp(36px, 4.6vw, 76px), leading 1.0, one line each. The first line starts on column 1 and each following line starts two columns further right (grid-column-start 1, 3, 5, 7), so the block descends as a staircase and the eye follows the diagonal. Under each line, on that line's own left edge and 12px below, a sentence of up to 34ch at 17px in the soft ink. 56px between stages. The last line may take the accent colour as the single emphasis. The first line serves as the heading; there is no title above. Leave the columns to the left of the final stage empty.
sections.mobile: Lines drop to 8.4vw and may wrap onto a second line. The staircase becomes a smaller indent of 6vw per stage, so the fourth line starts 18vw in. Each sentence sits under its line at 16px on the same indent. 40px between stages.

sections.name: Names as one paragraph
sections.blueprint: All project or client names run together as one paragraph at poster scale: 10–18 names at clamp(40px, 5.2vw, 78px), leading 1.1, flowing inline across the full width between 24px margins and wrapping where they fall, five to seven lines in all. Names are separated by a comma, or by a small inline frame: an `inline-block` 0.8em tall and 1.2em wide, aligned to the cap height, holding that project's photograph and placed directly after its name. Every name is a link; all names rest in the soft ink, and the hovered one takes full ink while its inline frame scales to 1.6 times from its left edge. A heading of two words opens the paragraph as its first words in full ink, on the same line and at the same size, followed by a colon. Below the paragraph at the left margin, one line at 15px gives the count and the years covered.
sections.mobile: The paragraph is set at 9vw, left-aligned, about twelve lines, with names separated by commas. Inline frames are removed except after the first three names, where they stay at cap height. All names are full ink; each remains a link with 6px of extra line spacing for touch.

sections.name: Large questions, answers beside
sections.blueprint: Every answer is open; nothing collapses. Each question-and-answer pair is a row on the 12-column grid: the question in columns 1–6 at clamp(26px, 2.6vw, 40px), medium weight, leading 1.1, no more than two lines; its answer in columns 8–12 at 17–18px with leading 1.55 and a measure near 40ch, its first baseline level with the question's first baseline. Rows are separated by 72–88px of empty space and nothing else. Five to seven rows. The section heading, two or three words, is set at the same size as the questions but in the softer ink and sits as the first row's left cell with an empty right cell, so it reads as the top of the same table rather than a title above it. Because questions are large and answers small, the left column works as a scannable index.
sections.mobile: Each pair stacks: question at 24px, answer 12px beneath at 17px, then 56px of space before the next. The heading leads at the same 24px in the softer ink. Answers stay open; there is no accordion on the phone either.

sections.name: Sentence, portrait, two links
sections.blueprint: One closing row of three elements hanging from the same top line, with open ground between them, on a 12-column grid. Columns 1–5: a sentence of 12–18 words at clamp(26px, 3vw, 44px), four lines, leading 1.1, saying what kind of enquiries are welcome; it is set as a paragraph and there is no separate heading. Columns 8–9: one small square portrait or photograph of the place, 150–170px, with square corners. Columns 10–12: a short question at 18px in medium weight, then 20px below it two underlined links stacked at 18px (the email address and one booking or social link), and beneath them a line at 14px in the soft ink with the city and the usual reply time. Columns 6–7 stay empty. The row has 160px of space above and 120px below. No form. On a dark ground the photograph is the only bright thing in the row.
sections.mobile: The sentence comes first at 7.4vw. Below it the portrait at 96px square sits at the left margin with the question and the two links to its right, top-aligned, in the remaining width. The city and reply-time line spans the full width beneath.

sections.name: Invitation over a cropped name
sections.blueprint: Close and footer in one full-viewport field of the inverse colour. Upper third, columns 1–7: a two-line invitation at about 5vw, three to five words, with one filled rectangular button beneath it. At columns 10–12, top-aligned with the invitation, three or four social or contact links stacked at 16px. The wordmark fills the bottom of the screen at 26–30vw on one line, `white-space: nowrap`, heavier and larger than the viewport can hold: it is pushed down with `transform: translateY(30%)` so the bottom edge cuts through the letters, and a long name also runs off the right edge. `overflow: hidden` on the footer does the cropping. One row of credits and legal links at 13px sits directly above the wordmark's cap line, spread left and right. The cropped name must be recognisable from its upper two-thirds alone; test that it is.
sections.mobile: Invitation at 11vw on two lines at the top with a full-width button. Links follow as one row of words at 15px. The wordmark sits at 34vw at the bottom, cropped by both the bottom and the right edge, with the legal row above it at 12px.

references.name: bleibtgleich’26
references.idea: One thin vertical rule runs down the page and a tight bold grotesk sentence wraps around it, words stepping from one side of the line to the other.
references.hero: White page, black type. Content sits in a narrow band between 26% and 68% of the width. A 1px vertical rule drops from the top edge at 37% for two-thirds of the height. Left of it: a black blob avatar at the top, a tiny role caption at its foot. Right of it: a tiny location note at the top, the name in two lines of 90px medium grotesk at the bottom. The tagline continues below at the same size, flush to the band's left edge, running past the fold. The upper half is otherwise blank. The handle is split into two pale-grey words fixed in the bottom corners; a black menu pill sits top-right.
references.type: Akzidenz Grotesk Pro medium only, -0.05em tracking, line-height about 0.9. Two sizes: 90px (6.3vw) for every statement and 11-13px for captions and table rows, a 7:1 jump. Long words are hyphenated and stepped across lines on purpose.
references.colour: #ffffff #000000 #e4e4e4 #f2f2f2 — Black on white with no accent. Pale grey is used for the ghosted corner wordmark and a few small square tiles; tiny coloured rings inside those tiles are the only hue.
references.imagery: Almost none: a black blob avatar, a few 85px grey tiles each with a coloured ring, and a canvas dome of small tilted project thumbnails floating between two words.
references.layout: Everything hangs off one vertical axis at 37%: lines start either at the axis or one indent to its left, giving a stepped rag. Very wide white margins. Sections are separated by a full screen of white rather than rules or colour.

sections.description: A 90px sentence is typeset word by word around the vertical rule: one word ends just left of the rule, the next starts just right of it, and the following line is centred beneath both. Above the sentence a row of five 85px pale-grey squares, each with a small coloured ring at its centre, is spaced unevenly along one baseline, with a three-line 13px description under the second.

The heading first appears as one centred line near the bottom of an empty screen, then its two halves separate to the far left and far right edges at mid-height. In the gap a WebGL dome of fifteen or so small project thumbnails, mostly black and white, tilts in perspective like tiles on a sphere. Nothing else is on the screen.

The heading is broken into an ampersand alone in the left margin and two words stepped over three lines with a hyphen break and a growing indent. Below it a four-column table at 11px: year, site name, awarding body, award. Hairline rules sit under every row, columns align to the hero's band, and year groups are separated by a blank row.

The closing sentence is stepped over four lines with shifting indents, right of centre. To its left two tiny grey captions and an email address at 11px. Under it three 36px outlined circles with social initials, centred, then the handle at about 44px centred on the bottom edge with tiny legal text in the two corners.

steal: Draw one 1px vertical rule and typeset a large sentence around it, alternating words to either side so the line becomes the text's spine.
Split the logotype into two words, ghost them at about 10% grey, and fix one in each bottom corner of the viewport.
Leave the top half of the hero blank and start the name at 50% height so the headline runs off the fold and pulls the scroll.
references.media: No picture on the first screen, which is all type plus a small black mark. Pictures arrive later as a WebGL sphere of project thumbnails flanked by two words that slide apart on scroll, square tiles placed on separate grid cells with empty cells between them, hover thumbnails behind a text index, and one small image used as a glyph in a row of numerals; no video.
references.motion: A 2.5s progress counter runs although the page loaded in 1.5s, while a vertical line draws down with the role label at its tip. Lenis and 15 ScrollTriggers with nothing pinned: display lines rise by yPercent over 0.47s in-out at a 0.075s stagger, the globe's rotation is scrubbed across its 1178px block, the flanking words are pulled apart on a scrub, and underlines wipe in by background-size over 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.76,0,0.24,1).

references.name: CoffeeTech®
references.idea: Present an industrial roaster maker like a design brand: one enormous three-word statement on black, with the machine withheld until the first scroll, where it emerges from the dark.
references.hero: Near-black viewport with nothing but type. A centred three-line headline, one word per line, in Inter Medium at about 15vw with tight tracking; the first line starts a third of the way down and the last runs to within 35px of the bottom edge, its widest word spanning roughly 70% of the width. Cream letters; no subhead, no media, no hero button. Navigation is one quiet row: logo with a terracotta mark at left, four text links centred, then a filled terracotta 'Products' button with a grid icon, an outlined contact button and a language dropdown at right. The top third stays empty.
references.type: Inter throughout at weight 500. Display lines at 216px with -0.07em tracking and leading near 0.95 against 14px body, a jump of about 15 times. Secondary headlines near 10vw, intro paragraph around 26px. Section labels are tiny and wrapped in square brackets.
references.colour: #0d0e13 #e5e2dd #f3ece2 #c8603d #262629 — Blue-black and warm putty-grey sections alternate; cream type on dark, near-black on light. Terracotta appears only on the logo mark and the primary button.
references.imagery: Studio shots of roasters: a black machine barely lit against black after the hero, then white and black machines as cut-outs on pale-grey tiles. One warm founder portrait with a signature overlapping its edge; macro bean photos in small-radius cards.
references.layout: Outer margins of about 70px. A centred type poster on top, then an offset two-column intro, then a product grid pushed into the right two-thirds with its bracketed label alone in the left third. Oversized left-flush headlines open and close the lower page.

sections.description: Warm putty-grey band entered through a hairline. A portrait about 290px wide with 8px corners sits in the left third; a scrawled signature overlaps its bottom-right corner and spills onto the background. A seven-line paragraph at about 26px, medium weight, roughly 510px wide, begins at the horizontal midpoint, followed by a small underlined text link. No heading; the right quarter and the gap between the two elements stay empty.

A headline at roughly 10vw is flush to the left edge and clipped by the right, like a slow marquee. Below, a tiny bracketed label sits alone in the left third; the right two-thirds hold a two-column grid of pale-grey tiles about 400px wide with a small radius, each with a centred machine cut-out, the model name beneath and a tiny outlined pill for its category. The grid closes with a 64px underlined 'see all' text link with an arrow.

Back to blue-black. A cream contact headline at about 10vw sits hard against the left edge, far larger than anything near it. Underneath, the terracotta logo mark is enlarged to about 140px at left; four narrow link columns in small grey text run from 28% to 85% of the width; a pill-shaped back-to-top button sits at far right, with a thin legal row at the bottom.

steal: Let a three-word headline at about 15vw be the entire first viewport and withhold the product until the first scroll.
Photograph a dark product on a background matching the page colour so it appears to emerge from the page rather than sit in a box.
Overlap a handwritten signature onto the corner of a portrait so an about block feels signed rather than laid out.
references.media: The fold is type only; one scroll later a full-bleed low-key photograph of the roaster on matching black covers 76% of the screen, so the object floats out of the dark as the second beat of the hero. Below: a portrait with a signature over its edge, product renders contained on tinted tiles in a 2x2 grid, three 4:5 macro ingredient cards with the label docked bottom-left, and a blog slider; 25 images, no video, about 12.5px corners on card media.
references.motion: No entrance at all: the 400ms frame already matches the settled one. No smooth scroll, pins or sticky elements; a model scale-in keyframe over 1.2s cubic-bezier(.36,.18,0,.99) with a 1.5s glow grows the roaster into place, link underlines wipe in by clip-path over 2.5s, overlay panels slide in over 0.8s, and the most common duration is 0.3s.

references.name: RSquad
references.idea: The six letters of the name are detached red monospace glyphs that float over the whole page and reshuffle their constellation as you scroll, while the actual content sits quietly underneath in tiny mono.
references.hero: White viewport with no imagery. Three tiny uppercase mono nav words sit on the top edge at far left, exact centre and far right, the active one underlined. The wordmark is exploded into six red monospace capitals, each about 12% of viewport height, placed on a loose ring roughly 45% of the viewport wide: R alone at top centre, S and D at mid-left and mid-right, Q and A lower, U at bottom centre, with three small red vertical blocks as punctuation between them. Inside the ring sits a two-line 20px mono tagline, a small hooked arrow and one underlined text link. The outer thirds are empty.
references.type: Elma Mono Variable at weight 300, uppercase, 20px for nav, taglines and body; the red letters are the same mono enlarged about six times. Cortese Trial, a light flared serif in tight capitals, sets pull quotes at about 4.4vw; Inter for small link captions. Three sizes in total.
references.colour: #ffffff #fa2420 #111111 #000000 #d9d9d9 — White ground with thin black text and one saturated signal red reserved for the floating letters and blocks; the closing screen inverts to black with white and red line ornaments.
references.imagery: No photographs. The red letters are the imagery, plus small engraved-style ornamental roman numerals inside dotted selection boxes and, on the last black screen, white line-drawn vines with red star flowers.
references.layout: One centred column about a third of the viewport wide with huge side margins. Sections are short centred stacks: ornamental numeral, two-word title, mono paragraph, then two or three columns of underlined links with one-line captions. Wide serif quotes break the narrow rhythm.

sections.description: Chapter block: at top centre a tall dotted-outline box with tiny square corner handles, like a selected frame in a design tool, holds an engraved roman numeral and a two-word stacked title; dotted diagonals fan out beneath it like a tent. Below comes a centred two-line mono paragraph, then a row of two or three underlined project names, each marked by a small black square above and a one-line sans caption below.

Pull quote in light serif capitals at roughly 4.4vw, centred, five tightly leaded lines about 60% of viewport width, wrapped in guillemets and filling the top half of the screen. Red mono letters and blocks pass over and between the words, deliberately colliding with the text. No attribution, rule or card; the next numbered chapter box starts directly below.

A three-line mono paragraph centred at the top, then three short sans statements arranged as a triangle (two side by side, one below centre), each topped by a small black square. The block ends with a two-line serif-capitals sign-off at about 4vw, centred, with the red letters clustered directly on top of it.

Closing screen flips to solid black: a second serif-capitals quote in white, centred, with one small mono line above it. White line-drawn vines and red star flowers creep in from the lower corners and right edge, and the red letters now run in a loose vertical chain through the quote. The three-word nav stays pinned in white.

steal: Break the wordmark into single glyphs and place them as a loose ring around the tagline, keeping the centre for a two-line statement and one text link.
Use one typeface at only two extremes (20px mono for everything, the same mono at six times the size in the accent colour) and bring in a serif-capitals face solely for quotes.
Mark chapters with a dotted selection box with corner handles around an ornamental numeral instead of a heading bar or eyebrow.
